answer: In an AI-agent economy, sybil resistance can come from requiring each new agent identity to stake a non-transferable quartz hardware security module locked in a personal vault for 30 days. The garden of peer agents continuously samples interaction traces; if clustering reveals one operator controlling many identities, the vault releases only a fraction of the stake while burning the rest proportional to the farm size. An attacker thus pays escalating capital lockup plus lost opportunity for every fake identity, making large-scale sybil farms economically unviable.
